title: Galaktoboureko: Semolina Custard Filo Pie with Lemon Syrup
summary: A golden filo pie hiding a thick semolina custard, soaked in a fragrant lemon syrup while still hot from the oven.
equipment: deep 25 cm round or square baking tin

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring 1000 ml whole milk to the boil in a heavy saucepan.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Lower the heat right down and rain in 100 g fine semolina, whisking constantly, then stir in 180 g caster sugar and simmer 5-6 min.

steps.title: Enrich
steps.text: Off the heat, beat in 120 g diced butter, then 4 eggs one at a time and 1 tsp vanilla, until the custard is thick, pourable and reaches 71 °C.

steps.title: Line
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C, butter a 25 cm tin and lay in 8 sheets of the 450 g filo, brushing each with 140 g melted ghee and letting the ends hang over the sides.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pour the custard into the filo case.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Cut the remaining filo to size, brush each sheet with ghee, stack on top, then brush and roll in the overhanging edges to seal.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Score the top in diamonds, sprinkle with a little water and bake about 1 h until light golden and set.

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Meanwhile simmer 600 ml water with 400 g sugar and half a lemon for about 1 h, then squeeze in the juice and discard the peel.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Pour the hot syrup over the pie as it comes out of the oven, keeping hands well clear as it bubbles up, then cool before cutting along the scored lines.

tips: Add the semolina to the milk very gradually over low heat, whisking the whole time, to keep it smooth and lump-free.
Check the custard reaches 71 °C before layering it into the filo so the eggs are properly cooked through.
Pour the hot syrup over the pie the moment it leaves the oven, standing well back as it bubbles up vigorously.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature or in the fridge for up to 3 days, and serve at room temperature or gently warmed.
